title: Optimal Search and Positive-Adversary Bounds with Accidentally Collapsing Measurements
description:
Research preprint, version 0.3.0. We study a hypothetical Born sampler that independently projects its sampled register with probability epsilon, with immediate outcome/flag feedback on the same persistent state and a noiseless input oracle. Constant-success unique-item search has optimal total query/readout/preparation/ordinary-measurement cost Theta(N^(1/3)+sqrt(epsilon N)), with separately paid gates, classical work, space, transcript bits and precision.

The revision adds a second main theorem: every finite Boolean promise problem with success at least 2/3 satisfies Q min{P+1,ceil(1/epsilon)} >= Adv_+(f)/36, using P+1 at epsilon=0. Adv_+ is the entrywise-nonnegative spectral adversary. A complete-history spectral query charge covers entangled workspace, partial measurements, permitted resets, feedback and unequal stopping without a history-count factor. Fixed and decreasing powers are proved separately. The parity application gives Omega(n) queries at any fixed positive collapse rate. The sharper search theorem is retained.

The algorithmic template, ideal endpoint and conditional-copy framework are attributed to ABFL and Miloschewsky--Podder; prior imperfect-readout robustness to Abbas et al.; positive weighted/spectral adversary machinery to the established literature including Miloschewsky--Podder and Spalek--Szegedy. Certificates may be exponentially large analytical objects. No signed-adversary extension, efficient certificate discovery, physical implementation, classification of all noisy PDQP or ordinary BPP/BQP result is claimed. OpenAI Codex assisted derivation, literature comparison, drafting and internal checking. Separate provider CLI AI-review reports and dispositions are archived; no independent human peer review or formal certification has occurred.
